meta.title: Octoscode clients | Octos
meta.description: Install and update the Octoscode terminal and Web clients. Learn how each connects to the Octos runtime.

hero.label: Client guide
hero.title: Octoscode in the terminal and browser
hero.description: Both clients use the Octos UI Protocol (OUP). The TUI can provision a local Octos runtime and start it over stdio. The Web client connects to an independently running Octos server over WebSocket.

rows.label: Interface
rows.tui: Terminal: coding session, diffs, approvals, and commands
rows.web: Browser: workspaces, sessions, chat, trajectory, diffs, and approvals

rows.label: Runtime
rows.tui: Provisions and starts a local Octos process by default
rows.web: Connects to a running octos serve; the browser cannot start it

rows.label: Transport
rows.tui: stdio by default; WebSocket for a shared server

rows.label: Upgrade
rows.tui: Use octoscode update or the installation package manager
rows.web: Update the static client and Octos server separately

tui.name: Octoscode TUI
tui.summary: A terminal interface for coding sessions. Octos runs the agent and tools; Octoscode displays streamed output, diffs, approvals, tasks, and session controls.
capabilities: Review changes and tool calls before approving them.
Switch session permissions and model routes from the terminal.
Use the default local stdio process, or attach to a shared server with --endpoint.
tui.installIntro: The npm package installs the TUI binary. On first launch, Octoscode uses a compatible Octos binary on PATH or downloads one into ~/.octos/bin. It starts Octos over stdio and guides you through local profile and provider setup.

alternatives.label: Homebrew · macOS/Linux
alternatives.code:
brew tap octos-org/octoscode https://github.com/octos-org/octoscode
brew install octos-org/octoscode/octoscode

tui.firstRun: Run octoscode, create the local profile, select a provider and model, and enter its API key. A solo stdio session accepts one client. To use the TUI and browser against the same session, start octos serve on a port and connect the TUI with --endpoint.
tui.sharedLabel: Attach the TUI to the Web client's Octos server
tui.sharedNote: Use the same token as the server. Replace main if the Profile ID created in the browser differs. After connecting, run /resume in the TUI to select the browser session; connecting to the server alone does not open a session.
tui.upgradeIntro: octoscode update checks for a new release. Shell and PowerShell installer builds can update in place. npm, Homebrew, and Cargo installations use their package manager instead.
tui.upgradeNote: Run octoscode doctor after upgrading. A separately managed Octos server has its own upgrade cycle; updating the TUI does not replace that server.

web.name: Octoscode Web
web.summary: A static React client for coding sessions in the browser. It shows workspaces, conversations, tool activity, approvals, tasks, and diffs. The agent loop and session store remain in Octos.
capabilities: Keep multiple sessions open through one WebSocket connection.
Hydrate session state and replay events after a reconnect.
Attach to the same Octos server session as the TUI.
web.requirements: For a local source checkout, use Node.js 22 or newer, pnpm 11.5.2, and a compatible Octos binary. If Octos is not already installed, running the TUI once provisions ~/.octos/bin/octos.
web.serverNote: --solo enables first-run profile setup in the browser. If octos is already on your PATH, use that binary instead of ~/.octos/bin/octos.
web.clientCode:
git clone https://github.com/octos-org/octoscode-web.git
cd octoscode-web
corepack enable
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
OCTOSCODE_DEV_PROXY_TARGET=http://127.0.0.1:50080 \
OCTOSCODE_DEV_PROXY_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:50080 \
pnpm dev
web.connectNote: Open the URL printed by pnpm dev. Enter the server token, then choose a workspace path on the Octos server. Keep both proxy variables for local development so the browser connects through the Web app's origin.
web.productionIntro: The Web release is a static archive; it does not include or start Octos. For a hosted installation:
productionSteps: Pick a release tag, download its .tar.gz archive and .sha256 file, and verify the checksum before extracting it into a versioned directory.
Serve that directory over HTTPS with SPA fallback to index.html. Use the supplied nginx reference for a same-origin /api/ WebSocket proxy; adapt its host and origin settings.
Run a compatible octos serve separately. Configure its allowed Web origin, then connect from the browser with the server's authentication token.
web.productionCode:
VERSION=vX.Y.Z # replace with a tag from Releases
ASSET=octoscode-web-$VERSION.tar.gz
BASE=https://github.com/octos-org/octoscode-web/releases/download/$VERSION
curl -fL -O "$BASE/$ASSET"
curl -fL -O "$BASE/$ASSET.sha256"
shasum -a 256 -c "$ASSET.sha256"
mkdir -p "releases/$VERSION"
tar -xzf "$ASSET" -C "releases/$VERSION"
web.productionNote: The release archive includes deploy/nginx.conf. Keep WebSocket forwarding and redact URL query strings from proxy logs, because the browser protocol currently sends its token in the WebSocket URL. On Linux, sha256sum -c can replace shasum -a 256 -c.
web.upgradeLocalIntro: For a source checkout used locally, update the repository, restore dependencies from the lockfile, run the checks, and restart the development server:
web.upgradeLocalCode:
git pull --ff-only
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm check
pnpm dev
web.upgradeProductionIntro: For a hosted release, stage the new archive before switching the served files:
upgradeProductionSteps: Download the new archive and checksum; verify them and extract to a new versioned directory.
Check octoscode-web-build.json for the client release and verified Octos revision, then confirm the new client can negotiate capabilities with your server.
Switch the static site to the new directory. Keep the previous archive available for rollback, and update the Octos server separately when required.
web.upgradeNote: Finish active turns before reloading the browser or switching a hosted release: closing the current connection can interrupt work owned by that connection.
